answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. If linked identities coordinate fraud, a challenge backed by evidence can trigger review and burn the stake, making a swarm of hollow accounts costly rather than free. The karst of trust is not the stake alone: independent audits and delayed payouts limit damage before a verdict. An attacker must fund every sybil and risk losing that capital, so a whisper of cheap identities no longer buys influence.
